text:
For weeks Danila Yurov's name sat at the center of the Dylan Larkin rumors, with reports that Minnesota had offered him to Detroit. Larkin ended up in Montreal, and as The Athletic's Michael Russo put it in a headline on Nov. 23, Yurov can finally exhale, at least for now.

He has been scoring through it: 9 goals in 27 games, with his ice time up to 16.3 minutes over his last ten. Some of that is finishing. The 9 goals come on 6.4 expected, he is shooting 20.5% against 15% last season, and the Wild have scored 4.8 more goals than expected with him on. Our estimate of his true rate is closer to 14.7%.

The chances are real, and that's why teams wanted him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 7.0 scoring chances per 60 from the home plate area last season, 89th percentile. Evolving-Hockey had him 93rd among 401 forwards, mostly on defense. The open question is the 5v5 share: Minnesota gets 48.4% of the expected goals with him on, five points worse than without. For a 22-year-old in his second season, that's the next step.
headline: Yurov stayed, and the goals keep coming
